meta.audience: The reader, addressed as Gentiles in verse 11
meta.location: The valley of Nimrod, the wilderness, and Moriancumer
principles: A migration guided by a voice in a cloud
A decree attached to a land
A problem the Lord hands back

world_behind.title: The valley is named for a hunter
world_behind.text: Verse 1 says Nimrod, called after the mighty hunter.

world_behind.title: They carry a whole ecology
world_behind.text: Verses 2 and 3 list fowls, fish, deseret the honey bee, and seeds of every kind. 1 Nephi 8:1 and 16:11 have Lehi's party carrying seeds too, and Ether 6:4 adds flocks and herds. Two migrations six hundred years apart are provisioned the same way, and only this one names the bee.

world_behind.title: A word is translated for the reader
world_behind.text: Verse 3 says deseret means a honey bee.

world_behind.title: The Lord travels with them unseen
world_behind.text: Verses 4 and 5 have him talk from a cloud, and the brother of Jared does not see him.

world_behind.title: Moroni breaks in
world_behind.text: Verses 9 through 12 leave the narrative to address the Gentiles about the decree on this land. Ether 4:6, Ether 5:1, Ether 8:20 to 26 and Ether 12:6 are his other interruptions, so Moroni steps out of the Jaredite story five times in fifteen chapters.

world_behind.title: Four years pass without prayer
world_behind.text: Verse 14 has the Lord chasten him for three hours because he remembered not to call upon his name. It is the only rebuke of the brother of Jared in the record, and it falls between Ether 1:34 to 43, where his praying gets a whole people moved, and Ether 3, where it gets him a vision.

world_behind.title: The chapter ends on a question
world_behind.text: Verse 25 has the Lord ask what the brother of Jared wants him to do about the light. 1 Nephi 17:9 has Nephi ask the reverse question, where to find ore for the ship, so the two ocean crossings put the question in opposite directions.

words.text: The name of a valley, given after the mighty hunter. The record uses the name four times and the King James Bible four, including Genesis 10:9.
Traps for catching birds or animals. The record uses the word four times and the King James Bible fifteen. Verse 2 has them catching fowls of the air.
A word the record translates as honey bee. It appears once, here, and in no other book.
Flat vessels for carrying loads on water. The record uses the word five times, three of them in this chapter, and the King James Bible not at all.
Corrected, disciplined. Treated at 1 Nephi 16:25. The word turns up five times here, and the King James Bible eight.
Brought to a point. The record uses the word once, here, while the King James Bible has none. Verse 17 uses it of the ends of the barges.
A great sea creature. Its count is twice, here and at Ether 6:10, in this book, while the King James Bible three times. Verse 24 uses it of how they will ride the water.

phrases.term: The name of the valley was Nimrod, being called after the mighty hunter
phrases.text: An aside explaining a place name. Genesis 10:9 supplies the man.

phrases.term: Deseret, which, by interpretation, is a honey bee
phrases.text: The record translating its own vocabulary. It is the only occurrence of the word.

phrases.term: He was in a cloud, and the brother of Jared saw him not
phrases.text: The form the guidance takes. Verse 5 says the Lord went before them and gave directions the same way.

phrases.term: Into that quarter where there never had man been
phrases.text: The destination described by absence. No one has been there.

phrases.term: Whoso should possess this land of promise... should serve him, the true and only God, or they should be swept off
phrases.text: The decree in one sentence. Verses 9 and 10 restate it twice more.

phrases.term: The fulness of his wrath cometh upon them when they are ripened in iniquity
phrases.text: The timing built into the decree. Verse 10 says it is not until the fulness of iniquity.

phrases.term: This cometh unto you, O ye Gentiles, that ye may know the decrees of God
phrases.text: Moroni turning to his reader. He applies the Jaredite terms to the people who will hold the book.

phrases.term: They dwelt in tents upon the seashore for the space of four years
phrases.text: The gap in the story. Verse 14 says what was missing during it.

phrases.term: Chastened him because he remembered not to call upon the name of the Lord
phrases.text: The fault named exactly. Three hours of talking, over a lapse in praying.
The phrase repeated four times in a lone verse, of bottom, sides, top, and door. The description works by repetition.

phrases.term: What will ye that I should do that ye may have light in your vessels?
phrases.text: The question that turns the problem back. Verse 25 asks it again after ruling out windows and fire.

verses.label: v. 2–3
verses.title: A packing list, and a word given twice
verses.text: The record itemises the migration by what was carried: fish kept alive in "a vessel, in which they did carry with them the fish of the waters," fowls caught in snares, "seeds of every kind," flocks and herds. In the middle of the list sits a word left in its own language and then translated in the same clause: "they did also carry with them deseret, which, by interpretation, is a honey bee." A record that leaves neas and sheum unglossed at Mosiah 9:9 supplies the meaning here, in the same breath as the term.

verses.label: v. 5
verses.title: A destination defined by the absence of people
verses.text: The record gives the destination no name and no direction, only a description: "the Lord commanded them that they should go forth into the wilderness, yea, into that quarter where there never had man been." The place is identified by what has not happened in it. Nothing in the chapter locates it any further, and the same verse adds that they went "being directed continually by the hand of the Lord," so the route is not specified either.

verses.label: v. 8–13
verses.title: A digression the record marks at both ends
verses.text: Five verses break out of the narrative and address a reader who is not in it: "this cometh unto you, O ye Gentiles, that ye may know the decrees of God, that ye may repent, and not continue in your iniquities until the fulness come." The tense shifts to the present and the subject becomes the land itself, "a land which is choice above all other lands." Verse 13 closes the aside with a phrase that names it: "And now I proceed with my record." The writer signals his own interruption on the way out but not on the way in.

verses.label: v. 14
verses.title: A rebuke, and the record times it
verses.text: The correction is given a duration no summary needs: "the Lord came again unto the brother of Jared, and stood in a cloud and talked with him. And for the space of three hours did the Lord talk with the brother of Jared, and chastened him because he remembered not to call upon the name of the Lord." The offence is an omission over four years, and the record states both figures. What is reported is not the content of the rebuke but its length.

chapter.title: They carry the makings of a world
chapter.text: Verses 2 and 3 name birds, fish, bees, and seed. The migration is stocked to start over.

chapter.title: The record stops to translate a word
chapter.text: Verse 3 gives deseret as honey bee. The gloss is for the reader, not the travelers.

chapter.title: Guidance comes without a face
chapter.text: Verse 4 says he did not see him. The Lord leads from inside a cloud for the whole journey.

chapter.title: Moroni applies the decree to his own reader
chapter.text: Verse 11 addresses the Gentiles directly. The Jaredite terms are said to be the standing ones.

chapter.title: Four silent years are recorded as a fault
chapter.text: Verse 14 has the Lord rebuke him over the neglected prayer. The lapse is stated without softening.

chapter.title: The barges are described by repetition
chapter.text: Verse 17 says tight like unto a dish four times. The design is conveyed by insistence.

chapter.title: Two problems get different treatment
chapter.text: Verse 20 solves the air problem outright; verse 23 hands the light problem back.

chapter.title: The chapter ends unresolved
chapter.text: Verse 25 is a question. The answer belongs to the next chapter and to the man who was asked.

applications.title: Pack for the place you are going
applications.text: They carried bees and seed. What you bring decides what is possible when you arrive.

applications.title: Expect guidance you cannot see
applications.text: He talked from a cloud for the whole journey. Direction and visibility are separate things.

applications.title: Practise on the small crossings
applications.text: They built barges and crossed many waters in the wilderness long before the ocean vessels were begun. The hard version of a task tends to arrive for people who have already done the easy version several times.

applications.title: Notice a long stretch without praying
applications.text: Four years passed and the correction took three hours. Drift is quiet while it happens.

applications.title: Bring both problems at once
applications.text: He reports no light and no air inside the same prayer. Listing everything that is wrong beats raising one item and saving the rest for a second conversation.

applications.title: Some problems get solved outright
applications.text: The air is answered directly, with a hole in the top and one in the bottom and instructions for when the water comes in. Two difficulties were raised, and only one of them is handed back to him.

applications.title: Take the stated constraints as the design brief
applications.text: He is told there can be no windows, since they would be dashed in pieces, and no fire. Being told what will not work narrows the search, and what he eventually brings lives inside those limits.

applications.title: Answer the question you are handed
applications.text: The Lord asked him what to prepare. Being asked back is a form of being trusted.

questions.text: What am I carrying that I will need later?
Where am I being sent that no one I know has been?
What have I been given on terms I have stopped reading?
Which warning meant for someone else applies to me?
How long has it been, honestly?
What problem has an obvious answer I have not asked for?
What is God waiting for me to propose?

entries.head: Ether 1:38

anchor.quote: which was choice above all other lands, which the Lord God had preserved for a righteous people

entries.reason: the land Jared had wondered aloud about

targets.quote: a land which is choice above all the earth?
targets.verse_text: And it came to pass that Jared spake again unto his brother, saying: Go and inquire of the Lord whether he will drive us out of the land, and if he will drive us out of the land, cry unto him whither we shall go. And who knoweth but the Lord will carry us forth into a land which is choice above all the earth? And if it so be, let us be faithful unto the Lord, that we may receive it for our inheritance.
targets.markdown: And it came to pass that Jared spake again unto his brother, saying: Go and inquire of the Lord whether he will drive us out of the land, and if he will drive us out of the land, cry unto him whither we shall go.
